title: Instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis for a man with ALS
summary: A brain-computer interface decoding 256 microelectrodes in the ventral precentral gyrus synthesized the participant's intended voice causally, with a reported latency of about 10 ms per decoding step. Listeners understood almost 60% of synthesized words, compared with 4% when he was not using the device, and he could modulate intonation and sing short melodies. Caveat: a single participant with ALS, within the BrainGate2 trial, and the authors describe the technology as early stage.
ai_technology: Deep neural network speech decoder for intracortical recordings
organization: UC Davis; Stanford University; BrainGate consortium

evidence.tested: A single participant with ALS used a neural decoder on 256 microelectrodes with closed-loop audio feedback to produce synthesized voice in near real time, and could modulate intonation and sing short melodies.
evidence.unknown: A single participant within a trial; the abstract states no explicit limitations, and the authors describe the technology as early stage.
evidence.ai_role: A neural decoder translated attempted-speech activity into synthesized voice; the abstract does not say whether it uses machine learning.
